question: Does a verified filesystem compile-cache hit prepare the Jev adapter request faster than recompiling it locally?
providerEconomics: unknown: no provider request is made, so provider tokens, cached tokens and cost are null
limitations: Offline, single host, single process; not a production latency claim.
Jev compiles locally by serializing the question, so the compile being avoided is cheap.
Provider-prefix reuse and provider-qualified economics are out of scope here and tracked in #2683.
